testimonials.text: How the intervention timing and specificity could have such an effect on preventing long term disability in the patient. Being quizzed on the depth of burns as we went was very helpful.

The part I found interesting was the primary and secondary survey then the part of fluid resuscitation and the hours to give and also when there's delayed presentation. I now understand how to calculate the fluid better.
I usually work in IPD and seen the burn case after primary management. So this course made me know what are the primary management, adhoc managements of burn and also about the escharotomy.

The most interesting aspects were the practical, real-life approach to burn resuscitation in resource-limited settings. Specifically, the concepts of early hypotension is never burn shock, the correct use of the patient's own hand for 1% TBSA, and when to consider escharotomy for painful deep circumferential burns. The distinction between primary, secondary, and tertiary prevention was also very clarifying.

What I found most interesting was the practical approach to burn care, especially TBSA estimation, early fluid resuscitation, and timing of excision and grafting. The focus on prevention and challenges in low-resource settings was also very insightful.
Chapter 4 is amazing, all the different cases and photos showing different presentations and different types and depths, very informative for assessing burns. Loved.
